definitions.explanation: Trust or confidence placed in a person, especially in a political or organizational context. Often refers to the formal trust bestowed upon a leader, diplomat, or official.

examples.japanese: {内閣|ないかく}{信任|しんにん}{案|あん}が{可決|かけつ}された。
examples.english: The vote of confidence in the cabinet was passed.

examples.japanese: {大使|たいし}は{信任|しんにん}{状|じょう}を{提出|ていしゅつ}した。
{国民|こくみん}の{信任|しんにん}を{得|え}るために、{首相|しゅしょう}は{解散|かいさん}{総選挙|そうせんきょ}に{踏|ふ}み{切|き}った。
examples.english: To gain a mandate from the people, the prime minister decided on a snap general election.

notes:
A formal political and diplomatic term.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {信任|しんにん}を{得|え}る (gain confidence/trust)
- {信任|しんにん}{状|じょう} (credentials — diplomatic document)
- {信任|しんにん}{案|あん} (vote of confidence)
- {不信任|ふしんにん}{案|あん} (vote of no confidence)
- {不信任|ふしんにん}{決議|けつぎ} (no-confidence resolution)

The opposite, {不信任|ふしんにん} (no confidence), is more commonly seen in news, as votes of no confidence are more newsworthy than votes of confidence.
